environment: local built Worker, local D1, synthetic data
limits: Local built Worker with the Sites dispatcher header model; this proves server-side authorisation of the implemented routes, not the hosted Cloudflare Access sign-in (see identity-hardening).

Requests are built from the route parameters read from the route readers in lib/saha/*-server.ts; a route reader that adds a parameter must be added to ROUTE_PARAMS here (the suite fails on an unclassified route).

Seven roles in one organisation: owner (clinician with owner authority), admin, supervisor, two ASHAs, clinician, and a stranger. The provider role, delegation and emergency-access paths are not exercised here.
A response is judged by status and by searching its text for synthetic patient names and identifiers; a leak of an unnamed derived value (a count, a village) would not be found.

Commands: a representative set (27 rows in the command table) across patient, organisation, owner-only, import and identity families, not the 211 command names in docs/current/COMMAND-CATALOGUE.csv; the role refusals are asserted; for owner-only commands whose valid input needs configuration this suite does not build, the owner receives a validation or state answer (404, 409 or 422), which is recorded but not judged.

measures.label: ms from suspension acknowledgement to the first denied request (BRD limit 5 minutes)

checks.label: route catalogue is fully classified (every GET route in HTTP-ROUTES.csv has documented parameters here)
grid is complete: 68 requests x 8 principals, every cell has a status
control: owner gets 2xx on legacy routes and403 on the exact ASHA-only Today/Routine contracts
Today list allows both active ASHAs and refuses all other roles; ASHA 2 opens its own record
control: for every ASHA-readable route naming a resource of ASHA 2, ASHA 2 gets 200 (so ASHA 1's refusal is a scope refusal, not a malformed request)
clinical source history permits scoped clinicians and refuses both ASHAs including the assigned ASHA
inbound conflict history permits scoped care clinicians and supervisor and refuses ASHAs and administrator
frozen figure metadata permits current reporting owner/supervisor and refuses other roles
bounded action-review index permits only its assigned ASHA
(i) no route returns 5xx for any role or anonymously
(ii) anonymous gets 401 on every GET /api/ route
(iii-a) the stranger never gets 2xx for this organisation (every GET route refuses with 403)
(iii-b) no response to the stranger (success or error) carries this organisation's id, name, patients, visits, media or members
(iv-a) ASHA 1 asking for ASHA 2's patient, visit or media gets 403 or 404 on every such route
(iv-b) on every route, ASHA 1 never receives ASHA 2's patient names, patient ids, visit ids or media id, and ASHA 2 never receives ASHA 1's
(v-a) the admin (no patient scope) never receives a patient name on any route
(v-b) the admin gets 403 or 404 on every route that names a patient, visit or media item
(vi) no response carries an invitation token or its stored hash (searched by value, for every principal)
(vii) every API response is Cache-Control: no-store
work-burden policy requires current care membership for every role
work-burden report is operations-only for every current role
availability report is operations-only for every current role
value range publication report is owner/clinician-only for every current role
Routine grid permits exactly assigned ASHA2 and refuses owner authority and every other role
Routine successful contexts bind exact current person/visit/org/trusted actor with no-store and preserve clinical state
Routine malformed/duplicate/foreign selectors refuse error-only without another person or visit disclosure
(ii) anonymous gets 401 on every POST and DELETE /api/ route, except signature-authenticated callbacks
(ii) the MIS webhook refuses an unsigned anonymous call (4xx, never 2xx or 5xx)
(ii) the reminder callback refuses an unsigned anonymous call (4xx, never 2xx or 5xx)
POST /api/record-opened: ASHA 2, the owner, the clinician and the supervisor may report opening ASHA 2's patient; ASHA 1, the admin and the stranger are refused
POST /api/patients (name search): each role finds only the patients it may see; the admin and the stranger find none
POST /api/patient-matches: asking with ASHA 2's patient's exact name and locality reveals the match only to roles in scope; ASHA 1, the admin and the stranger learn nothing
POST /api/media and DELETE /api/media/<id> on ASHA 2's draft visit: ASHA 1, the admin and the stranger are refused, and ASHA 2's media survives
